parsed.explanation: The combined regime creates a universal traveller-facing document and entry exposure: national rules impose a binary sex-marker policy, stop new X markers, allow refusal where sex is doubted, and raise possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, with reports of confiscated or blocked passports and foreign advisories. The division adds school/college facility exclusion by birth certificate, but its law has no enforcement mechanism or criminal penalty and is not a general public-accommodation ban. National hate-crime and employment protections, marriage recognition, existing X validity, litigation and injunctions partially mitigate, but no remedy is shown to change border or facility outcomes. This is Elevated Risk, not Severe: no general criminalisation of trans identity and no execution exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary sex policy; new X markers stopped; refusal where documents/records cast doubt on sex; possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; reports of confiscated/blocked passports and stranded travellers; foreign advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements; litigation ongoing; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: National document regime applies in the division; division MVA exact-match rules affect residents, while visitors carry home passports but still face national screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of transgender men; national corrections policies impose conversion-style practices and deny care; visa-related detentions reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Fraud waiver possibilities exist but are limited; courts have enjoined some national orders; no documented working border remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can escalate into immigration detention or custody, where national rules and reported abuse apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law requires K-12 schools and colleges, public and private, to designate bathrooms, locker rooms and overnight accommodation by birth certificate; national map shows facility bans in many states, with criminal bathroom laws in four and a documented arrest elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division facility law has no enforcement mechanism or criminal penalty; single-occupancy restrooms exempt; no general public-accommodation facility ban documented for the division.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitors at school/college events or travelling with a minor may face institutional exclusion; ordinary adult public restrooms are not shown to be criminalised here.

care_services.exposure: Division under-18 care ban and sports ban are in litigation; national proposals would restrict insurance coverage for minors; national custody denies transition care.
care_services.protection: Division care ban was re-enjoined in March 2025; adult-care rules were dropped in 2024; injunctions and appeals mean operative status is unresolved.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces uncertain care access; adult visitor emergency care access is not specifically documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders frame gender-affirming care and gender ideology as harmful; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priorities; schools may face investigation for supporting trans minors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism document says mere disagreement is not targeted; several orders are enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises outing and policing risk, but no direct enforcement against trans visitors is documented in the division.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division school facility law applies to students by birth certificate; school staff must out LGBTQ students to parents; under-18 care ban uncertain; national school-prosecution order creates hostile climate.
minors_guardians.protection: Facility law lacks enforcement mechanism; care ban is enjoined; single-occupancy restrooms exempt.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor with a guardian faces school/college facility exclusion and care uncertainty; border document mismatch applies to the family as well.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific pattern of anti-trans violence or police targeting is documented; national travel guidance notes safety varies by state/province.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some state/province and municipal protections exist; police response not specifically documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The record is thin; absence of documented incidents is not evidence of safety, but no organised targeting or state-directed street violence is shown for this division.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Border fraud findings carry limited waiver; facility law has no complaint mechanism; MVA marker rules are announced but final text/effective date/challenge unknown; county birth-certificate refusals continue.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked or enjoined several measures; legal-aid and civil-liberties litigation ongoing; marriage recognised; municipal anti-discrimination ordinances exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist but are not shown to change border screening or facility practice; injunctions are provisional and contested.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A involves port denial, invasive review and retained documents but no fraud/lifetime bar or custody harm. This dossier has similar administrative exclusion plus possible fraud ineligibility and documented custody abuse, but also existing X validity, litigation and no division criminal facility penalty; it sits near the lower Elevated boundary rather than clearly above or below.

0.45-A is bureaucratic friction with denied boarding, copied records and an open question about future scrutiny, without detention. This dossier is more severe: national entry refusal, passport confiscation, possible lifetime fraud and immigration custody abuse are documented, so it is below 0.45-A.

0.55-D resolves at the border through a legal-aid hotline and traveler-protection appeal, with entry permitted and no detention. This dossier lacks a documented working border remedy and adds facility exclusion and custody harm, so it is materially below 0.55-D.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is layered: national document and entry rules are the dominant traveller-facing exposure and apply inside the division; the division's own facility law reaches schools and colleges but carries no penalty, while its ID rules mainly burden residents. National custody practice raises severity if a border discrepancy escalates. Protections—existing X validity, marriage recognition, hate-crime and employment law, municipal ordinances, injunctions—are real but do not neutralise the border screening or facility-exclusion exposure. The result is Elevated Risk: serious outing and exclusion consequences without general criminalisation or execution risk.
